2. The respondent as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 89 of 1993 before the Senior Assistant Judge, Karimganj, District Kishoreganj for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of 0.04 acres of viti land with a tin shed alleging, inter alia, that the defendant sold 0.04 acres of viti land along with a tin shed thereon at a consideration of Tk. 99,000/- to the plaintiff by a registered sale deed dated 29.3.1990 with an agreement of reconveyance executed and registered on the same day. The time of reconveyance was 3 months. But the defendant did neither hand over physical possession of the said property nor returned the money to the plaintiff as per agreement dated 29.3.1990 in-spite of repeated requests of the plaintiff. So the plaintiff issued a legal notice to the defendant on 6.3.93 stating all the facts and circumstances and the plaintiff also stated that if the defendant failed to pay the said amount within 1(one) month from the date of receipt of the said notice, the plaintiff will file a suit for appropriate relief. But the defendant after receipt of the said notice did not take any step. 

 3. The petitioner being the defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations contending, inter alia, that the defendant sold the suit land. So, the conditional sale will be treated as a usufructuary mortgage and as such the suit in its present form is not maintainable and the plaintiff is not entitled to get any declaration of title and recovery of khas possession of the suit land. 

 7. Mr.Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate appears on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Shamsuddin Bulbul, the learned Advocate appears on behalf of the respondents. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the courts below failed to consider the evidence on record and arrived at erroneous conclusion. The learned Advocate further submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the plaintiff purchased the suit land on 29.3.1990 from the defendant-petitioner and on the same date the plain-tiff executed and registered a deed of agreement with a condition that if the defendant paid back the said consideration money within 3 (three) months from the date of execution of sale deed. then _the plaintiff shall be bound to re-convey the suit land and thus Section 95A of the S.A. & T Act, 1950 any conditional sale will be treated as 'usufructuary mortgage and hence the impugned judgment of the High Court Division suffers from misconception of law The learned Advocate also submits that the 'High Court Division failed to appreciate the facts that the sale was conditional one with an agreement to re-convey and it constituted a usufructuary mortgage for which no suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession is maintainable.
